segments: Tenth Dynasty.
Arabian kings.
Ayyub is a great and blessed house,
and all the brothers, nephews, cousins, and their sons ride with two thousand horsemen.
And do not think that I am their enemy;
believe that I am not their enemy,
but rather their friend and a fighter on their behalf.
For there is an alliance by marriage between us,
and my uncle also was their brother-in-law.
And it is fitting for you to make friendship with them,
so that we and they may be enemies to your enemies."
The Khwarazmshah, however, was obstinate and replied
that he could not abandon Khilat,
and he intensified the battle against it.
Then certain people of Van acted treacherously and surrendered the city,
and the Khwarazmians took control over it.
And the brothers of al-Ashraf fled,
as well as Husam al-Din Qaimari, al-Ashraf's brother-in-law by his maternal sister,
and 'Izz al-Din Aybak, the governor of Khilat,
and they took refuge in the fortress of Khilat.
And after some days, they obtained a promise for their lives,
and surrendered the fortress.
Now, when the Khwarazmshah captured Khilat,
he did not imprison the brothers of al-Ashraf,
but they entered his service,
riding with him
and playing games before him every day in the hippodrome.
Now when al-Ashraf heard, he was shaken,
and he set out in haste and arrived at Ablastein,
and his forces gathered to him {OCR?}.
Sultan 'Ala al-Din also set out with his forces,
and they all gathered in Aqshahr (or Akshahr).
And the Khwarazmshah also, when he heard,
went with his forces to meet them.
And they were forty thousand.
And they found about four thousand horsemen of the Rhomaeans who were separated from their companions,
and they killed them all.
And they drew near again, and the armies clashed with one another on Friday,
and the victory belonged to Malik al-Ashraf.
And they remained the whole night of Saturday devastating and being devastated.
And when Saturday morning dawned,
the battle was set in array,
and a great slaughter fell upon the Khwarazmians,
and a vast number of them were killed,
whose count no man was able to determine;
and certain satraps and men of renown were also captured.
